# SailPoint Developer Community

> Documentation, API references, SDKs, and guides for building on SailPoint Identity Security Cloud, IdentityIQ, and Non-Employee Risk Management.

##### Operations

- [Account Attribute](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/account-attribute.md): Look up an account for a particular source on an identity.
- [Base64 Decode](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/base64-decode.md): Render base64 data in its original binary format.
- [Base64 Encode](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/base64-encode.md): Encode data with a Base64-based text encoding scheme.
- [Concatenation](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/concatenation.md): Join two or more string values into a combined output.
- [Conditional](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/conditional.md): Output different values depending on simple conditional logic.
- [Date Compare](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/date-compare.md): Compare two dates and return a calculated value.
- [Date Format](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/date-format.md): Convert datetime strings from one format to another.
- [Date Math](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/date-math.md): Add, subtract, and round components of a timestamp's incoming value.
- [Decompose Diacritical Marks](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/decompose-diacritical-marks.md): Clean or standardize symbols used within language.
- [Display Name](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/display-name.md): Use Preferred Name over Given Name to create an identity’s Display Name.
- [E.164 Phone](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/e164-phone.md): Convert a phone number string into an E.164-compatible number.
- [First Valid](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/first-valid.md): Return the first piece of data that is not null.
- [Generate Random String](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/generate-random-string.md): Generate a random string of any length.
- [Get End of String](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/get-end-of-string.md): Get the rightmost N characters of a string.
- [Get Reference Identity Attribute](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/get-reference-identity-attribute.md): Get another user's identity attribute.
- [Identity Attribute](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/identity-attribute.md): Get a user's identity attribute's value.
- [Index Of](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/index-of.md): Get the location of a specific substring within a value.
- [ISO3166](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/iso-3166.md): Convert a string into an ISO 3166 country code value.
- [Join](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/join.md): Join two or more string values into a combined output with a defined separator.
- [Last Index Of](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/last-index-of.md): Returns last location of specific substring.
- [Left Pad](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/left-pad.md): Left pad of the input string.
- [Lookup](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/lookup.md): Look up and return a key's matching value.
- [Lower](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/lower.md): Convert an input string into all lowercase letters.
- [Name Normalizer](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/name-normalizer.md): Clean or standardize the spelling of strings coming in from source systems.
- [Random Alphanumeric](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/random-alphanumeric.md): Generate a random string of any length.
- [Random Numeric](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/random-numeric.md): Generate a random number of any length.
- [Reference](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/reference.md): Reuse a transform that has already been written.
- [Replace All](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/replace-all.md): Find and replace all instances of all patterns.
- [Replace](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/replace.md): Find and replace all instances of a single string.
- [RFC5646](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/rfc-5646.md): Convert three-letter abbreviation to RFC5646 language tag.
- [Right Pad](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/right-pad.md): Add padding to the right of an incoming string.
- [Rule](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/rule.md): Reuse rule logic that has already been written for a previous use case.
- [Split](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/split.md): Return the Nth element of a split array.
- [Static](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/static.md): Return a fixed string value.
- [Substring](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/substring.md): Get the inner portion of a string passed into the transform.
- [Trim](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/trim.md): Trim whitespaces from both the beginning and ending of input strings.
- [Upper](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/upper.md): Convert an input string into all uppercase letters.
- [Username Generator](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/username-generator.md): Derive a unique value for an attribute in an account create profile.
- [UUID Generator](/docs/extensibility/transforms/operations/uuid-generator.md): Create a universal unique ID (UUID).

#### Rules


##### Guides

- [Your First Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/guides/your-first-rule.md): Learn to build your first rule!

##### Cloud Executed Rules

- [Account Profile Attribute Generator](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/account-profile-attribute-generator.md): This rule generates complex account attribute values during provisioning, e.g. when creating an account.
- [Account Profile Attribute Generator (from Template)](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/account-profile-attribute-generator-template.md): This rule generates complex account attribute values during provisioning, e.g. when creating an account.
- [Before Provisioning Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/before-provisioning-rule.md): This rule runs before provisioning to a source.
- [BuildMap Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/buildmap-rule.md): This rule manipulates raw input data provided by the rows and columns in a file.
- [Correlation Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/correlation-rule.md): This rule associates or correlates an account to an identity, based on complex logic.
- [Identity Attribute Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/identity-attribute-rule.md): This rule calculates and returns an identity attribute for a specific identity.
- [Manager Correlation Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/manager-correlation-rule.md): This rule calculates a manager relationship between identities.
- [Transform Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/cloud-rules/transform-rule.md): This rule performs transforms.

##### Connector Executed Rules

- [Before and After Rule Operations](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/before-and-after-rule-operations.md): This rule executes PowerShell commands on the IQService component after a source account has an operation performed on it.
- [JDBC BuildMap Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/jdbc-buildmap-rule.md): This rule manipulates raw input data provided by the rows and columns in a file and builds a map from the incoming data.
- [JDBC Provision Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/jdbc-provisioning-rule.md): This rule performs provisioning actions from a provisioning plan provided by a supplied JDBC connection. These actions typically issue SQL commands, such as insert, update, select, and delete.
- [SAP BuildMap Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/sap-buildmap-rule.md): This rule gathers additional attributes from SAP systems to build accounts. This rule is implemented using SAP's Java Connector (JCo) framework provided by a supplied SAP connection.
- [SAP HR Provisioning Modify Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/sap-provisioning-modify-rule.md): This rule performs SAP HR modification operations during provisioning. This rule is typically used for attribute sync to custom SAP HR attributes.
- [Web Services After Operation Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/webservices-after-provisioning-rule.md): This rule calculates attributes after a web-service operation call.
- [Web Services Before Operation Rule](/docs/extensibility/rules/connector-rules/webservices-before-provisioning-rule.md): This rule calculates attributes before a web-service operation call.
- [SailPoint Human Fabric Rule Utility](/docs/extensibility/rules/rule-utility.md): Using IdnRuleUtil as a Wrapper for Common Rule Operations
- [Java Docs](/docs/extensibility/rules/java-docs.md): Documentation for rule development in IdentityNow.

#### Event Triggers

- [Trigger Types](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/trigger-types.md): These are the different trigger types you can use.
- [Preparing a Subscriber Service](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/preparing-subscriber-service.md): Before you can subscribe to an event trigger, you must prepare a service that can accept incoming HTTP requests from the event trigger service.
- [Subscribing to a Trigger](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/subscribing-to-trigger.md): Usually, you will subscribe to event triggers using the user interface in SHF. Refer to subscribing to event triggers to learn how to subscribe to an event trigger through the SHF UI.
- [Filtering Events](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/filtering-events.md): Many triggers can produce a staggering amount of events if left unfiltered. Event filtering helps you solve this problem.
- [Testing Triggers](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/testing-triggers.md): It is important to test your trigger subscription configuration with your actual subscribing service before enabling your subscription for production use.
- [Responding to Response Required Triggers](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/responding-request-response-trigger.md): Specify how your application interacts with response required type trigger services.

- [Account Deleted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/account-deleted.md): Fires after an account is deleted.
- [Account Updated](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/account-updated.md): Fires after an account is updated.
- [Campaign Activated](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/campaign-activated.md): Triggered when a campaign is activated.
- [Campaign Ended](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/campaign-ended.md): Triggered when a campaign is ended.
- [Campaign Generated](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/campaign-generated.md): Triggered when a campaign finishes generating.
- [Certification Signed Off](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/certification-signed-off.md): Triggered when a certification is signed off by its reviewer.
- [CIEM Auto-Include Scope Setting Changed](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/ciem-auto-include-scope-setting-changed.md): Fires after a user enables or disables the Auto-Include Scope setting for a CIEM source.
- [CIEM New Scope Detected](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/ciem-new-scope-detected.md): Fires after a new AWS account, Azure subscription, or GCP project is detected by SailPoint CIEM.
- [CIEM Scope Selection Changed](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/ciem-scope-selection-changed.md): Fires after a user changes the scope selection for a CIEM source.
- [Form Submitted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/form-submitted.md): Triggered when a form is submitted.
- [Identity Attributes Changed](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/identity-attribute-changed.md): Fires after one or more identity attributes changed.
- [Identity Created](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/identity-created.md): Fires after an identity is created.
- [Identity Deleted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/identity-deleted.md): Fires after an identity is deleted.
- [Machine Identity Created](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/machine-identity-created.md): Fires after a machine identity is created.
- [Machine Identity Deleted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/machine-identity-deleted.md): Fires after a machine identity is deleted.
- [Machine Identity Updated](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/machine-identity-updated.md): Fires after a machine identity is updated.
- [Native Change Account Created](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/native-change-account-created.md): Fires after Account Aggregations detects that a new account is created external to Identity Security Platform on sources
- [Native Change Account Deleted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/native-change-account-deleted.md): Fires after Account Aggregations detects that an account is deleted external to Identity Security Platform on sources
- [Native Change Account Updated](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/native-change-account-updated.md): Fires after an account is updated outside of Identity Security Platform
- [Outlier Detected](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/outlier-detected.md): Fires after an identity was detected as an outlier.
- [Provisioning Completed](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/provisioning-completed.md): Fires after a provisioning action completed on a source.
- [Scheduled Search](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/scheduled-search.md): Fires after a scheduled search completes.
- [Source Created](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/source-created.md): Fires after a source is created.
- [Source Deleted](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/source-deleted.md): Fires after a source is deleted.

- [VA Cluster Status Change](/docs/extensibility/event-triggers/triggers/va-cluster-status-change.md): Fires after the status of a VA cluster has changed.

##### in-depth

- [API Calls](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/api-calls.md): Calling API endpoints sequentially for hundreds or thousands of accounts is slow. If several API calls are required to build a user’s account, then it is recommended that you use asynchronous functions to speed up this task.
- [CLI - Advanced](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/cli-advanced.md): Using the CLI to properly test and debug your connector in SailPoint Human Fabric
- [HTTP Client](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/http-client.md): The connector SDK includes a built-in HTTP client with authentication, automatic retries, and logging. Use it to simplify API calls in your connectors.
- [Connector Timeouts](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/connector-timeouts.md): SailPoint Human Fabric will throw an error if your connector does not send a response in 3 minutes. For connector commands that might take longer than 3 minutes, make sure to send data at regular intervals to prevent a timeout.
- [Debugging](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/debugging.md): An easy way to debug locally is to use console.log() to print debug information to your console.
- [Error Handling](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/error-handling.md): If the code fails due to validation issues, connectivity, or configuration errors, you can handle the error and provide the user with information about what went wrong.
- [Linting](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/linting.md): Automatically check your connector source code for programmatic and stylistic errors.
- [Logging](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/logging.md): You can use this feature to read the logs of your connectors.
- [Caching](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/caching.md): The connector SDK provides an in-memory cache that persists across warm invocations. Use it to avoid redundant API calls and improve connector performance.
- [Data Store](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/data-store.md): The connector SDK provides a persistent data store backed by source connectorAttributes. Use it to store sync timestamps, pagination state, and other data that must survive connector restarts.
- [Handling Rate Limits](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/handling-rate-limits.md): Rate limiting for SaaS Connectivity.
- [Testing](/docs/connectivity/saas-connectivity/in-depth/testing.md): Testing SaaS Connectivity.
- [Filtering](/docs/tools/sdk/typescript/filter.md): Learn how to use the TypeScript SDK to filter results.

###### business_applications


###### Methods

- [BusinessApplications](/docs/tools/sdk/go/businessapplications/methods/business-applications.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status. Business Applications can be defined out-of-the-box, discovered from a source, or created by an administrator. Signatures on a Business Application drive automatic correlation of machine identities to it; sanctioned status is independent metadata that machine identities inherit once linked.

###### dimensions


###### Methods

- [Dimensions](/docs/tools/sdk/go/dimensions/methods/dimensions.md): Use this API to implement and customize dynamic role functionality. With this functionality in place, administrators can create dimensions and configure them for use throughout Identity Security Cloud. Identity Security Cloud can use established criteria to automatically assign the dimensions to qualified users. This enables users to get all the access they need quickly and securely and administrators to spend their time on other tasks. Entitlements represent the most granular level of access in Identity Security Cloud.

###### triggers


###### Methods

- [Triggers](/docs/tools/sdk/go/triggers/methods/triggers.md): Event Triggers provide real-time updates to changes in Identity Security Cloud so you can take action as soon as an event occurs, rather than poll an API endpoint for updates. Identity Security Cloud provides a user interface within the admin console to create and manage trigger subscriptions.  These endpoints allow for programatically creating and managing trigger subscriptions.

###### workflows


###### Methods

- [Workflows](/docs/tools/sdk/go/workflows/methods/workflows.md): Workflows allow administrators to create custom automation scripts directly within Identity Security Cloud.  These automation scripts respond to event triggers and perform a series of actions to perform tasks that are either too cumbersome or not available in the Identity Security Cloud UI.  Workflows can be configured via a graphical user interface within Identity Security Cloud, or by creating and uploading a JSON formatted script to the Workflow service.  The Workflows API collection provides the necessary functionality to create, manage, and test your workflows via REST.

###### business-applications


###### Methods

- [BusinessApplications](/docs/tools/sdk/powershell/businessapplications/methods/business-applications.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status. Business Applications can be defined out-of-the-box, discovered from a source, or created by an administrator. Signatures on a Business Application drive automatic correlation of machine identities to it; sanctioned status is independent metadata that machine identities inherit once linked.

###### dimensions


###### Methods

- [Dimensions](/docs/tools/sdk/powershell/dimensions/methods/dimensions.md): Use this API to implement and customize dynamic role functionality. With this functionality in place, administrators can create dimensions and configure them for use throughout Identity Security Cloud. Identity Security Cloud can use established criteria to automatically assign the dimensions to qualified users. This enables users to get all the access they need quickly and securely and administrators to spend their time on other tasks. Entitlements represent the most granular level of access in Identity Security Cloud.

###### triggers


###### Methods

- [Triggers](/docs/tools/sdk/powershell/triggers/methods/triggers.md): Event Triggers provide real-time updates to changes in Identity Security Cloud so you can take action as soon as an event occurs, rather than poll an API endpoint for updates. Identity Security Cloud provides a user interface within the admin console to create and manage trigger subscriptions.  These endpoints allow for programatically creating and managing trigger subscriptions.

###### workflows


###### Methods

- [Workflows](/docs/tools/sdk/powershell/workflows/methods/workflows.md): Workflows allow administrators to create custom automation scripts directly within Identity Security Cloud.  These automation scripts respond to event triggers and perform a series of actions to perform tasks that are either too cumbersome or not available in the Identity Security Cloud UI.  Workflows can be configured via a graphical user interface within Identity Security Cloud, or by creating and uploading a JSON formatted script to the Workflow service.  The Workflows API collection provides the necessary functionality to create, manage, and test your workflows via REST.

- [Business_Applications](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/methods/business-applications.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status. Business Applications can be defined out-of-the-box, discovered from a source, or created by an administrator. Signatures on a Business Application drive automatic correlation of machine identities to it; sanctioned status is independent metadata that machine identities inherit once linked.

###### Models

- [ArrayInner](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/array-inner.md): Properties
- [BaseReferenceDto](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/base-reference-dto.md): Properties
- [BusinessApplication](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status, either discovered from a source or defined by an administrator.
- [BusinessApplicationAdditionalOwnersInner](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application-additional-owners-inner.md): Properties
- [BusinessApplicationOrigin](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application-origin.md): How the Business Application entered the tenant catalog. Read-only; assigned by the service on creation and immutable thereafter.
- [BusinessApplicationOwner](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application-owner.md): Primary owner of the Business Application.
- [BusinessApplicationSignature](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application-signature.md): A (type, name) rule used to automatically correlate machine identities to this Business Application. A signature matches a machine identity when the identity's subtype equals type and its connector_attributes.spBusinessApplication equals name. Each (type, name) pair is unique across all Business Applications in the tenant; assigning a signature already owned by another Business Application returns a 409 conflict. Modifying signatures requires the custom Business Application feature to be enabled.
- [BusinessApplicationSource](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/business-application-source.md): Discovery source of the Business Application. null for out-of-the-box or administrator-defined Business Applications that were not discovered from a source.
- [DtoType](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/dto-type.md): An enumeration of the types of DTOs supported within the IdentityNow infrastructure.
- [ErrorMessageDto](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/error-message-dto.md): Properties
- [ErrorResponseDto](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/error-response-dto.md): Properties
- [JsonPatchOperation](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/json-patch-operation.md): A JSONPatch Operation as defined by RFC 6902 - JSON Patch
- [JsonPatchOperationValue](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/json-patch-operation-value.md): The value to be used for the operation, required for \"add\" and \"replace\" operations
- [ListBusinessApplicationsV1401Response](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/list-business-applications-v1401-response.md): Properties
- [ListBusinessApplicationsV1429Response](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/list-business-applications-v1429-response.md): Properties
- [LocaleOrigin](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/locale-origin.md): An indicator of how the locale was selected. DEFAULT means the locale is the system default. REQUEST means the locale was selected from the request context (i.e., best match based on the Accept-Language header). Additional values may be added in the future without notice.
- [SanctionedStatus](/docs/tools/sdk/python/business-applications/models/sanctioned-status.md): Indicates whether a Business Application is sanctioned for use within the organization. Machine identities linked to a Business Application inherit this value. Defaults to UNKNOWN when not explicitly set.

- [UsageType](/docs/tools/sdk/python/connectors/models/usage-type.md): The type of provisioning policy usage.  In IdentityNow, a source can support various provisioning operations. For example, when a joiner is added to a source, this may trigger both CREATE and UPDATE provisioning operations.  Each usage type is considered a provisioning policy.  A source can have any number of these provisioning policies defined.  These are the common usage types:  CREATE - This usage type relates to 'Create Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be created. For example, this would be used for a joiner on a source.   UPDATE - This usage type relates to 'Update Account Profile', the provisioning template for the 'Update' connector operations. For example, this would be used for an attribute sync on a source. ENABLE - This usage type relates to 'Enable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be enabled. For example, this could be used for a joiner on a source once the joiner's account is created.  DISABLE - This usage type relates to 'Disable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be disabled. For example, this could be used when a leaver is removed temporarily from a source. You can use these usage types for all your provisioning policy needs.

###### dimensions


###### Methods

- [Dimensions](/docs/tools/sdk/python/dimensions/methods/dimensions.md): Use this API to implement and customize dynamic role functionality. With this functionality in place, administrators can create dimensions and configure them for use throughout Identity Security Cloud. Identity Security Cloud can use established criteria to automatically assign the dimensions to qualified users. This enables users to get all the access they need quickly and securely and administrators to spend their time on other tasks. Entitlements represent the most granular level of access in Identity Security Cloud.

Subtype id. | Required | | SOURCE | DELETE | Derived from sourceId. | Required |

- [UsageType](/docs/tools/sdk/python/sources/models/usage-type.md): The type of provisioning policy usage.  In IdentityNow, a source can support various provisioning operations. For example, when a joiner is added to a source, this may trigger both CREATE and UPDATE provisioning operations.  Each usage type is considered a provisioning policy.  A source can have any number of these provisioning policies defined.  These are the common usage types:  CREATE - This usage type relates to 'Create Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be created. For example, this would be used for a joiner on a source.   UPDATE - This usage type relates to 'Update Account Profile', the provisioning template for the 'Update' connector operations. For example, this would be used for an attribute sync on a source. ENABLE - This usage type relates to 'Enable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be enabled. For example, this could be used for a joiner on a source once the joiner's account is created.  DISABLE - This usage type relates to 'Disable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be disabled. For example, this could be used when a leaver is removed temporarily from a source. You can use these usage types for all your provisioning policy needs.
- [Usagetypev2](/docs/tools/sdk/python/sources/models/usagetypev2.md): The type of provisioning policy usage.  In IdentityNow, a source can support various provisioning operations. For example, when a joiner is added to a source, this may trigger both CREATE and UPDATE provisioning operations.  Each usage type is considered a provisioning policy.  A source can have any number of these provisioning policies defined.  These are the common usage types:  CREATE - This usage type relates to 'Create Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be created. For example, this would be used for a joiner on a source.   UPDATE - This usage type relates to 'Update Account Profile', the provisioning template for the 'Update' connector operations. For example, this would be used for an attribute sync on a source. ENABLE - This usage type relates to 'Enable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be enabled. For example, this could be used for a joiner on a source once the joiner's account is created.  DISABLE - This usage type relates to 'Disable Account Profile', the provisioning template for the account to be disabled. For example, this could be used when a leaver is removed temporarily from a source. CREATEMACHINEACCOUNT - This usage type can be used to create the provisioning template for a source subtype which will be used in creating a machine account. You can use these usage types for all your provisioning policy needs.

###### triggers


###### Methods

- [Triggers](/docs/tools/sdk/python/triggers/methods/triggers.md): Event Triggers provide real-time updates to changes in Identity Security Cloud so you can take action as soon as an event occurs, rather than poll an API endpoint for updates. Identity Security Cloud provides a user interface within the admin console to create and manage trigger subscriptions.  These endpoints allow for programatically creating and managing trigger subscriptions.

###### workflows


###### Methods

- [Workflows](/docs/tools/sdk/python/workflows/methods/workflows.md): Workflows allow administrators to create custom automation scripts directly within Identity Security Cloud.  These automation scripts respond to event triggers and perform a series of actions to perform tasks that are either too cumbersome or not available in the Identity Security Cloud UI.  Workflows can be configured via a graphical user interface within Identity Security Cloud, or by creating and uploading a JSON formatted script to the Workflow service.  The Workflows API collection provides the necessary functionality to create, manage, and test your workflows via REST.

###### business_applications


###### Methods

- [BusinessApplications](/docs/tools/sdk/typescript/business_applications/methods/business-applications.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status. Business Applications can be defined out-of-the-box, discovered from a source, or created by an administrator. Signatures on a Business Application drive automatic correlation of machine identities to it; sanctioned status is independent metadata that machine identities inherit once linked.

###### dimensions


###### Methods

- [Dimensions](/docs/tools/sdk/typescript/dimensions/methods/dimensions.md): Use this API to implement and customize dynamic role functionality. With this functionality in place, administrators can create dimensions and configure them for use throughout Identity Security Cloud. Identity Security Cloud can use established criteria to automatically assign the dimensions to qualified users. This enables users to get all the access they need quickly and securely and administrators to spend their time on other tasks. Entitlements represent the most granular level of access in Identity Security Cloud.

###### triggers


###### Methods

- [Triggers](/docs/tools/sdk/typescript/triggers/methods/triggers.md): Event Triggers provide real-time updates to changes in Identity Security Cloud so you can take action as soon as an event occurs, rather than poll an API endpoint for updates. Identity Security Cloud provides a user interface within the admin console to create and manage trigger subscriptions.  These endpoints allow for programatically creating and managing trigger subscriptions.

###### workflows


###### Methods

- [Workflows](/docs/tools/sdk/typescript/workflows/methods/workflows.md): Workflows allow administrators to create custom automation scripts directly within Identity Security Cloud.  These automation scripts respond to event triggers and perform a series of actions to perform tasks that are either too cumbersome or not available in the Identity Security Cloud UI.  Workflows can be configured via a graphical user interface within Identity Security Cloud, or by creating and uploading a JSON formatted script to the Workflow service.  The Workflows API collection provides the necessary functionality to create, manage, and test your workflows via REST.

###### business_applications


###### Methods

- [BusinessApplications](/docs/tools/sdk/angular/business_applications/methods/business-applications.md): A Business Application groups machine identities (for example AI agents or applications) under a common owner and sanctioned status. Business Applications can be defined out-of-the-box, discovered from a source, or created by an administrator. Signatures on a Business Application drive automatic correlation of machine identities to it; sanctioned status is independent metadata that machine identities inherit once linked.

###### dimensions


###### Methods

- [Dimensions](/docs/tools/sdk/angular/dimensions/methods/dimensions.md): Use this API to implement and customize dynamic role functionality. With this functionality in place, administrators can create dimensions and configure them for use throughout Identity Security Cloud. Identity Security Cloud can use established criteria to automatically assign the dimensions to qualified users. This enables users to get all the access they need quickly and securely and administrators to spend their time on other tasks. Entitlements represent the most granular level of access in Identity Security Cloud.

###### triggers


###### Methods

- [Triggers](/docs/tools/sdk/angular/triggers/methods/triggers.md): Event Triggers provide real-time updates to changes in Identity Security Cloud so you can take action as soon as an event occurs, rather than poll an API endpoint for updates. Identity Security Cloud provides a user interface within the admin console to create and manage trigger subscriptions.  These endpoints allow for programatically creating and managing trigger subscriptions.

###### workflows


###### Methods

- [Workflows](/docs/tools/sdk/angular/workflows/methods/workflows.md): Workflows allow administrators to create custom automation scripts directly within Identity Security Cloud.  These automation scripts respond to event triggers and perform a series of actions to perform tasks that are either too cumbersome or not available in the Identity Security Cloud UI.  Workflows can be configured via a graphical user interface within Identity Security Cloud, or by creating and uploading a JSON formatted script to the Workflow service.  The Workflows API collection provides the necessary functionality to create, manage, and test your workflows via REST.
